```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, include = T, message = F, warning = F)
```

**This supplement contains the code and results for analyses based on alignment with only the 100 nations that have sample sizes larger than the number of parameters being estimated the Big Five model. To summarize, the trends are not appreciable different from the results in the full sample of 115 nations, and the focal trends generally become more stronger.**

# Analysis Code


## Load packages

```{r packages}
library(knitr) # for markdown stuff
library(countrycode) # to change country names easily
library(ade4) # to do pca with missing data
library(MplusAutomation) # to make preparing/manipulating mplus data/results easier
library(grid) # for customization of combined plots
library(maps) # for making maps
library(patchwork) # for combining plots
library(weights) # for removing leading zeros
library(gtsummary) # for prettier regrression tables
library(tidyverse) # for everything else
library(DT) # for searchable html tables
library(kableExtra) # other pretty tables

```


## IPIP-FFM cleaning and prep

```{r ipip_ffm}

# read in data from https://openpsychometrics.org/_rawdata/
ipip_ffm_raw <- read.delim("data/IPIP-FFM-data-8Nov2018/data-final.csv", stringsAsFactors = F)

ipip_ffm <-
  ipip_ffm_raw %>%
  filter(IPC == 1) # remove responses with duplicate IP address

og_n <- nrow(ipip_ffm_raw) # 1015341
ip_n <- nrow(ipip_ffm) # 696845
og_n - ip_n # 318496

ipip_include_countries <-
  ipip_ffm %>%
  mutate(country = forcats::fct_explicit_na(country)) %>%
  filter(country != "NONE") %>% # exclude responses from ps who had no country data available
  group_by(country) %>%
  summarise(n = n()) %>%
  filter(n >= 170)

ipip <- ipip_ffm %>% filter(country %in% ipip_include_countries$country)


ipip[, 1:50] <- data.frame(lapply(ipip[, 1:50], as.numeric))

# calculate acquiescence bias before recoding items using two opposite-valenced pairs from each factor
ipip$acquiescence_score <-
  rowMeans(ipip[, c(
    "EXT8",  # I don't like to draw attention to myself.
    "EXT9",  # I don't mind being the center of attention.
    "EST4",  # I often feel blue.
    "EST10", # I seldom feel blue.
    "AGR2",  # I am not really interested in others.
    "AGR7",  # I am interested in people.
    "CSN7",  # I like order.
    "CSN2",  # I leave my belongings around.
    "OPN6",  # I do not have a good imagination.
    "OPN3"   # I have a vivid imagination.
  )])

ipip_reverse_key <- read.csv("data/ipip_reversekey.csv", stringsAsFactors = F)

ipip_reverse_items <- c(ipip_reverse_key %>% 
                          filter(reverse == "yes") %>% 
                          select(item))$item

# reverse code necessary items
ipip[, ipip_reverse_items] <- 6 - ipip[, ipip_reverse_items]



# save cleaned data for faster loading
write.csv(ipip, "data/ipip_cleaned_data.csv")


(final_N <- nrow(ipip)) # n after exluding subjects from countries w/ fewer than 90 subjects
```

## Mplus alignment analysis

Run mplus input file named `Alignment.inp` in the folder called 'Alignment' and then come back. 

**(This analysis takes several days)**


## Import alignment results

Import alignment results and extract covariance and variance parameter estimates for meta-regression in Mplus.

```{r import_alignment, eval=T}


# import results file from alignment analysis
results <- readModels(target = "mplus/Alignment/Alignment_100_USAreference.out", 
                      filefilter = ".*knownclass")

# convert to somthing more useable
full_results <- 
  data.frame(results$parameters) %>% # make a data frame with just needed parameters
  # remove annoying constant prefix from names
  rename_all(.funs = funs(sub("unstandardized[.]", # part of name to remove
                              "", .))) # replace with nothing

# save alignment results dataframe for easier sharing and faster import than the raw txt file
write.csv(full_results, "data/full_alignment_results_USAref100.csv", row.names = F) 

```


```{r re_import}

full_results <- read.csv("data/full_alignment_results_USAref100.csv", stringsAsFactors = F) %>% 
  mutate_at(c('est', 'se', 'est_se', 'pval'), as.numeric)

```

## Country data tidying and Niche Diveristy PCA

```{r import_country_data, message=F}

UN_country_data <- read.csv("data/country_data/UN_country_data.csv")
Harvard_data <- read.delim("data/country_data/Harvard_rankings.tab")
english_proficiency_data <- read.csv("data/country_data/englishofficial_EPI_data.csv")
homicide_data <- read.csv("data/country_data/UNODC_homicide_rates.csv")
maleMortality_data <- read.csv("data/country_data/male_mortality.csv")
femaleMortality_data <- read.csv("data/country_data/female_mortality.csv")


index_year <- "X2015"

country_indices <- 
  UN_country_data %>% 
  filter(indicator_id %in% c(137506, # HDI
                             45106 # Urbanization
  )) %>% 
  select(indicator_name, iso3, index_year) %>% 
  spread(indicator_name, index_year) %>% 
  mutate(iso2 = countrycode(iso3, origin = "iso3c", 
                            destination = "iso2c"),
         iso3n = countrycode(iso3, origin = "iso3c", 
                             destination = "iso3n"),
         country = countrycode(iso3, origin = "iso3c", 
                               destination = "country.name"),
         continent = countrycode(iso3, origin = "iso3c", 
                                 destination = "continent")) %>% 
  select(country, iso2, iso3, iso3n, continent, 
         hdi = "Human Development Index (HDI)",
         urban_pop = "Urban population (%)") %>% 
  full_join(Harvard_data %>% 
              filter(year == 2015) %>% 
              select(iso3 = code, eci = hs_eci)) %>% 
  # homicide rate data from UNODC:
  # https://dataunodc.un.org/crime/intentional-homicide-victims
  full_join(homicide_data %>% 
  select(Region, Subregion, 
         country = UNODC.Name, 
         homicide_rate = X2015_ormostrecent) %>% 
      mutate(iso3 = countrycode(country, origin = "country.name", 
                                destination = "iso3c"),
             iso2 = countrycode(country, origin = "country.name", 
                            destination = "iso2c"),
         iso3n = countrycode(country, origin = "country.name", 
                             destination = "iso3n"),
         continent = countrycode(country, origin = "country.name", 
                                 destination = "continent"),
         country = countrycode(iso3, origin = "iso3c", 
                               destination = "country.name"),
         homicide_rate = as.numeric(as.character(homicide_rate))) %>% 
    # condense the estimates for UK into one estimate (there were four separate estimates)
    group_by(Region, Subregion, country, iso3, iso2, iso3n, continent) %>% 
    summarise(homicide_rate = mean(homicide_rate)) %>% ungroup()) %>% 
  full_join(maleMortality_data %>% 
              select(Country.Code, male_mortality = X2015_ormostrecent) %>% 
              full_join(femaleMortality_data %>% 
                          select(Country.Code, female_mortality = X2015_ormostrecent)) %>% 
              mutate(mortality = rowMeans(select(., male_mortality, female_mortality), 
                                          na.rm = T)) %>% 
              select(iso3 = Country.Code, mortality) %>% 
              mutate(iso2 = countrycode(iso3, origin = "iso3c", 
                                        destination = "iso2c"),
                     iso3n = countrycode(iso3, origin = "iso3c", 
                                         destination = "iso3n"),
                     country = countrycode(iso3, origin = "iso3c", 
                                           destination = "country.name"),
                     continent = countrycode(iso3, origin = "iso3c", 
                                             destination = "continent"))
  ) %>% 
  # join english proficiency data from: 
  # https://www.ef.edu/epi/downloads/
  full_join(
    english_proficiency_data %>% 
      select(country, iso3, EPI = EPI_mostrecent, english_official) %>% 
      mutate(iso2 = countrycode(country, origin = "country.name", 
                            destination = "iso2c"),
         iso3n = countrycode(country, origin = "country.name", 
                             destination = "iso3n"),
         continent = countrycode(country, origin = "country.name", 
                                 destination = "continent")) 
  ) 


```

```{r country_data_prepare}

country_df <- 
  ipip %>% 
  group_by(iso2 = country) %>% 
  summarise(N = n(),
            acquiescence = mean(acquiescence_score, na.rm = T)) %>% 
  mutate(acquiescence = scale(acquiescence, center = T, scale = T),
         iso3n = countrycode(iso2, origin = "iso2c", destination = "iso3n"),
         iso3 = countrycode(iso2, origin = "iso2c", destination = "iso3c"),
         country = countrycode(iso2, origin = "iso2c", destination = "country.name"),
         continent = countrycode(iso2, origin = "iso2c", destination = "continent")) %>% 
  full_join(country_indices) %>% 
  # add indices for places with personality data but no country-level 
  # hdi from https://www.unescap.org/sites/default/files/wp-09-02.tiff
  # urban population from https://www.worldometers.info/world-population/
  # Guam (316) - considered a US territory 
  mutate(hdi = ifelse(iso3n == 316, .901, hdi),
         urban_pop = ifelse(iso3n == 316, 94.5, urban_pop) # from 2015
         ) %>% 
  # Macao (446) - 'automonamous region' off coast of southern china
  mutate(hdi = ifelse(iso3n == 446, .933, hdi),
         urban_pop = ifelse(iso3n == 446, 99.8, urban_pop) # from 2015
         ) %>% 
  # Puerto Rico (630) - 'unincorporated' US territory
  mutate(hdi = ifelse(iso3n == 630, .905, hdi),
         urban_pop = ifelse(iso3n == 630, 97.4, urban_pop) # from 2010
         ) %>% 
  # Taiwan (158) - 'state in east asia'
    mutate(hdi = ifelse(iso3n == 158, .931, hdi),
           urban_pop = ifelse(iso3n == 158, 76.7, urban_pop)) # from 2015
      
# run pca on the three relevant variables
pca_miss <- nipals(df = scale(country_df %>% select(hdi, urban_pop, eci)), nf = 3) 
niche_diversity_scores <- pca_miss$li[,1] # scores on first composite = "socioecological complexity"


# variance explained by first composite
# first eigenvalue / sum(all eigenvalues) = variance explained by first component
pca_varexplained <- pca_miss$eig[1] / sum(pca_miss$eig)
pca_varexplained

pca_miss$co # loadings

# save scores to country data
country_df$niche_diversity <- niche_diversity_scores # niche_diversity  = niche diversity

# get china mortality to impute for Taiwan
china_mortality <- country_df %>% filter(country == "China") %>% pull(mortality)

# get highest EPI to impute for nations with english as official language but no EPI data
max_epi <-
english_proficiency_data %>% 
  filter(!is.na(EPI_mostrecent), english_official == 1) %>% 
  pull(EPI_mostrecent) %>% max

# get mean EPI for to impute for nations where english isn't an official language and no EPI data
mean_epi <-
english_proficiency_data %>% 
  filter(!is.na(EPI_mostrecent), english_official == 0) %>% 
  pull(EPI_mostrecent) %>% mean

country_data <- 
  country_df %>% 
  filter(!is.na(N)) %>% # remove countries where we dont have personality data from 
  # impute best guesses for the countries that don't have EPI data for any year
  mutate(mortality = ifelse(country == "Taiwan", china_mortality, mortality), 
         EPI = ifelse(is.na(EPI) & english_official == 1, 
                      max_epi, EPI), # if english is an official language
         EPI = ifelse(is.na(EPI) & english_official == 0, mean_epi, EPI)) %>%  # if not 
  # psych::describe() # to examine normality (looks like homicide rates are skewed and kurtotic)
  # log transform non-normal variables 
  mutate(homicide_rate = log(homicide_rate),
         logN = log(N)) 

```

```{r merge_alignment_country_data}
means <-

  mutate(param = paste(param, "mean", sep = "_"),
         est = as.numeric(est)) %>%
```

## Prepare metaregression data for Mplus

```{r metareg_mplus_prepare}

variances <- 
  full_results %>% # take dataset with all results 
  filter(paramHeader == "Variances") %>%  # keep only variance estimates 
  select(param, est, se, Group) %>% 
  mutate(iso2 = countrycode(Group, # mplus group (numeric country ID)
                            origin = "iso3n", # convert from number code
                            destination = "iso2c"), # to 2-character code
         est = as.numeric(est), # convert est column to numeric 
         se = as.numeric(se)) %>% 
  # join with country level data
  right_join(country_data, by = "iso2") %>% # country ID to join by 
  full_join(means) 

metareg_variance_mplusdata <- 
  variances %>% 
  # remove group that was fixed in alignment analyses
  filter(Group != 840) %>%  # (s.e. of 0 causes divide by zero error)
  select(variance = est, se, niche_diversity, iso3n = Group, continent, 
         N, logN, acquiescence, hdi, urban_pop, eci, 
         homicide_rate, mortality, EPI,
         contains("mean")) %>% 
  mutate(iso3n = as.numeric(iso3n),
         acquiescence = as.numeric(acquiescence),
         # Dummy codes for continent 
         Asia = ifelse(continent == "Asia", 1, 0),
         Africa = ifelse(continent == "Africa", 1, 0),
         Oceania = ifelse(continent == "Oceania", 1, 0),
         Americas = ifelse(continent == "Americas", 1, 0),
         num_continent = as.numeric(factor(continent))-1) %>% 
  select(-continent) 



# save dataframe for use in mplus metareg analysis
prepareMplusData(metareg_variance_mplusdata, 
                 "mplus/MetaRegression/metareg_variance_mplusdata.dat")


english_metareg_variance_mplusdata <- 
  variances %>% 
  # remove group that was fixed in alignment analyses
  filter(Group != 840) %>%  # (s.e. of 0 causes divide by zero error)
  filter(english_official == 1) %>% 
  select(variance = est, se, niche_diversity, iso3n = Group, continent, 
         N, logN, acquiescence, hdi, urban_pop, eci, 
         homicide_rate, mortality, EPI,
         contains("mean")) %>% 
  mutate(iso3n = as.numeric(iso3n),
         acquiescence = as.numeric(acquiescence),
         # Dummy codes for continent
         Asia = ifelse(continent == "Asia", 1, 0),
         Africa = ifelse(continent == "Africa", 1, 0),
         Oceania = ifelse(continent == "Oceania", 1, 0),
         Americas = ifelse(continent == "Americas", 1, 0),
         num_continent = as.numeric(factor(continent))-1) %>% 
  select(-continent) 

# save dataframe for use in mplus metareg analysis
prepareMplusData(english_metareg_variance_mplusdata, 
                 "mplus/MetaRegression/ENGLISH_metareg_variance_mplusdata.dat")

denominators <- # to standardize the covariances and get correlations later if needed
  full_results %>% 
  filter(paramHeader == "Variances") %>% # keep only variance estimates
  mutate(sd = sqrt(as.numeric(est))) %>% # sqrt of the variance = sd
  select(param, Group, sd) %>% # keep only vars that are needed
  spread(param, sd) %>% # to convert to wide format 
  # calculate denominator for standardizing the covariances into correlations
  # r = cov(x,y) / SD(x)*SD(y)
  mutate(O_C = O*C, # change namaes to match future correlation pair names
         O_E = O*E,
         O_A = O*A,
         O_ES = O*ES,
         C_E = C*E,
         C_A = C*A,
         C_ES = C*ES,
         E_A = E*A,
         E_ES = E*ES,
         A_ES = A*ES) %>% 
    select(Group, O_C:A_ES) %>% 
    gather(pair, denominator, -Group)
  
covariances <- 
  full_results %>% 
  # keep only the correlation parameter estimates
  filter(grepl('.WITH', paramHeader)) %>% 
  # combine columns to show what the pairwise correlation is
  unite(pair, paramHeader:param, sep = ".") %>% 
  mutate(pair = gsub(".WITH.", "_", pair), # replace mplus terms with snake_case for corrs
         iso2 = countrycode(Group, # mplus group (numeric country ID)
                             origin = "iso3n", # convert from number code
                            destination = "iso2c"), # to 2-character code
         est = as.numeric(est)) %>% # convert est column to numeric
  rename(covariance = est) %>% 
  mutate(se = as.numeric(se)) %>% 
  # merge with denominator data
  full_join(denominators) %>% 
  #calculate correlations from covariances and denominators
  mutate(correlation = covariance / denominator) %>% 
  # combine with country-level data (e.g., socioecological complexity)
  right_join(country_data, by = "iso2") %>% # country ID to join by 
  full_join(means)

# prepare this df for the meta-regression in mplus
metareg_covariance_mplusdata <- 
  covariances %>% 
  select(covariance, correlation, se, niche_diversity, iso3n = Group, continent, 
         # control variables
         N, logN, acquiescence, hdi, urban_pop, eci,
         homicide_rate, mortality, EPI,
         contains("mean")) %>% # mean IPIP factor scores for each country
  mutate(iso3n = as.numeric(iso3n), 
         acquiescence = as.numeric(acquiescence),
         abscov = abs(covariance), abscor = abs(correlation),
         # Dummy codes for contients
         Asia = ifelse(continent == "Asia", 1, 0),
         Africa = ifelse(continent == "Africa", 1, 0),
         Oceania = ifelse(continent == "Oceania", 1, 0),
         Americas = ifelse(continent == "Americas", 1, 0),
         num_continent = as.numeric(factor(continent))-1) %>% 
  select(-continent)

# save data for use in metareg
prepareMplusData(metareg_covariance_mplusdata, 
                 "mplus/MetaRegression/metareg_covariance_mplusdata.dat")

# prepare this df for the meta-regression by scaling standard errors 
scaled_metareg_covariance_mplusdata <- 
  covariances %>% 
  mutate(se = se / denominator) %>% # scale se by variance to make sure it doesnt change results
  select(covariance, correlation, se, niche_diversity, iso3n = Group, continent, 
         # control variables
         N, logN, acquiescence, hdi, urban_pop, eci, 
         homicide_rate, mortality, EPI,
         contains("mean")) %>% # mean IPIP factor scores for each country
  mutate(iso3n = as.numeric(iso3n), 
         acquiescence = as.numeric(acquiescence),
         abscov = abs(covariance), abscor = abs(correlation),
         # Dummy codes for continents
         Asia = ifelse(continent == "Asia", 1, 0),
         Africa = ifelse(continent == "Africa", 1, 0),
         Oceania = ifelse(continent == "Oceania", 1, 0),
         Americas = ifelse(continent == "Americas", 1, 0),
         num_continent = as.numeric(factor(continent))-1) %>% 
  select(-continent)

# save data for use in metareg
prepareMplusData(scaled_metareg_covariance_mplusdata, 
                 "mplus/MetaRegression/SCALED_se_metareg_covariance_mplusdata.dat")

# prepare this df for the meta-regression in mplus
english_metareg_covariance_mplusdata <- 
  covariances %>% 
  filter(english_official == 1) %>% 
  select(covariance, correlation, se, niche_diversity, iso3n = Group, continent, 
         # control variables
         N, logN, acquiescence, hdi, urban_pop, eci, 
         homicide_rate, mortality, EPI,
         contains("mean")) %>% # mean IPIP factor scores for each country
  mutate(iso3n = as.numeric(iso3n), 
         acquiescence = as.numeric(acquiescence),
         abscov = abs(covariance), abscor = abs(correlation),
         # Dummy codes for continents
         Asia = ifelse(continent == "Asia", 1, 0),
         Africa = ifelse(continent == "Africa", 1, 0),
         Oceania = ifelse(continent == "Oceania", 1, 0),
         Americas = ifelse(continent == "Americas", 1, 0),
         num_continent = as.numeric(factor(continent))-1) %>% 
  select(-continent)

# save data for use in metareg
prepareMplusData(english_metareg_covariance_mplusdata, 
                 "mplus/MetaRegression/ENGLISH_metareg_covariance_mplusdata.dat")


# For sensitivity analysis:
# check if absolute values,
# which may violate assumptions of sampling variability,
# alters results. 
# Need to see which pairwise covariances are on average negative 
# and scale them by multiplying those by -1. 
# But if the average covariance for a pair is positive, 
# then should leave the negative estimates as negative.

# find the pairs that are negative mean covariance
negative_covariances <-
covariances %>% group_by(pair) %>% 
  summarise(covariance = mean(covariance), 
            correlation = mean(correlation)) %>% 
  filter(covariance < 0) %>% 
  pull(pair)

# multiply those by -1 but leave the ones that are on average positive alone
reverse_scaled_covariances <-
  covariances %>%  
  mutate(covariance = ifelse(pair %in% negative_covariances, -1*covariance, covariance),
         correlation = ifelse(pair %in% negative_covariances, -1*correlation, correlation))

# merge with the other country data and prepare for mplus
negative_scaling_metareg_covariance_mplusdata <- 
  reverse_scaled_covariances %>% 
  select(covariance, correlation, se, niche_diversity, iso3n = Group, continent, 
         # control variables
         N, logN, acquiescence, hdi, urban_pop, eci, 
         homicide_rate, mortality, EPI,
         contains("mean")) %>% # mean IPIP factor scores for each country
  mutate(iso3n = as.numeric(iso3n), 
         acquiescence = as.numeric(acquiescence),
         # Dummy codes for continents
         Asia = ifelse(continent == "Asia", 1, 0),
         Africa = ifelse(continent == "Africa", 1, 0),
         Oceania = ifelse(continent == "Oceania", 1, 0),
         Americas = ifelse(continent == "Americas", 1, 0),
         num_continent = as.numeric(factor(continent))-1) %>% 
  select(-continent)

# save data for use in metareg
prepareMplusData(negative_scaling_metareg_covariance_mplusdata, 
                 "mplus/MetaRegression/negative_scaling_metareg_covariance_mplusdata.dat")




```


## Mplus meta-regression analyses

Run all the Mplus metaregression analyses using MplusAutomation: 

```{r run_metareg_mplus, message=F}
runModels(target = paste(getwd(),"mplus/MetaRegression/", sep = "/"), # need full file path
          replaceOutfile="always") #alternative: 'modifiedDate'
```

### Covariance and Variance Results

#### Baseline results (no controls)

```{r plot_results}

# plot covariance relationship with predicted values and confidence intervals

full_cov_output <- readModels(target = "mplus/MetaRegression/metareg_alignmentCovariances_base.out")

R2 <- full_cov_output$parameters$r2[[2]]
b <- full_cov_output$parameters$stdyx.standardized[2, 3]
pval <- full_cov_output$parameters$stdyx.standardized[2, 6]

eq <- substitute(italic(beta)~"="~ b*","~~italic(p)~pval* ","~~italic(R)^2~"="~r2,
```

### Effective Dimensionality Results

Function to estimate effective dimensionality and correct for small sample bias from: Del Giudice, M. (2020). Effective dimensionality: A tutorial. Multivariate Behavioral Research.

Code for function available at: https://figshare.com/articles/R_function_for_effective_dimensionality_ED_estimation_v_1_/11954661

```{r estimateED_function, include=F}
#
# estimate.ED
#
# Marco Del Giudice (2020). Version 1. Contact: marcodg@unm.edu
#
# A simple R function to compute estimates of effective dimensionality (ED), either from raw data or from a correlation/covariance matrix. The function returns four estimators, both uncorrected and corrected for small-sample bias if enough information is available. Disattenuated estimates can also be computed if desired, by supplying a vector of reliability coefficients. For more information see Del Giudice (2020).
#
# ED estimators: The n1 index is suitable as a general-purpose estimator of ED (Cangelosi & Goriely 2007, Roy & Vetterli 2007, Gnedenko & Yelnik 2016); n2 is more conservative and can be used as a lower bound estimate of dimensionality (Fraedrich et al. 1995, Bretherton et al. 1999, Pirkl et al. 2012). The estimators nC (Cheverud 2001, Wagner et al. 2008) and nInf (Kirkpatrick et al. 2009) are not recommended, and are only reported for comparison with the published literature. Whereas nC typically overestimates ED, nInf is extremely conservative and insensitive to changes in the correlation structure.  
#
# Small-sample correction: if raw data are supplied, the function uses the nlshrink package (Ramprasad 2016) to perform nonlinear shrinkage of the eigenvalues (Ledoit & Wolf 2012, 2015). If only the correlation or covariance matrix is supplied, the function applies the correction method by Mestre (2008). If the corrected ED is lower than the uncorrected ED (which may happen when the uncorrected ED is very close to the number of variables), the uncorrected value is returned in place of the corrected one. IMPORTANT: implementing Mestre's method is tricky; sometimes, the uniroot.all function may fail to find the correct mu values. When applying the small-sample correction to a correlation/covariance matrix, please check the results for unexpected or implausible values.
#
# Disattenuation: to correct for measurement error, disattenuated estimates of ED can be obtained by supplying a vector of reliability coefficients (e.g., Cronbach’s α, McDonald's omega-t or omega-h). For details see Del Giudice (2020). 
#
# Note: If the matrix supplied by the user is indefinite (or becomes indefinite after disattenuation), Higham's (2002) method is automatically applied to replace it with the nearest positive definite matrix (Matrix package by Bates & Maechler, 2019). A warning message is displayed in the output summary.
#
#
# References:
# Bates, D., & Maechler, M. (2019). Matrix v. 1.2-17. URL: https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=Matrix 
# Bretherton, C. S., Widmann, M., Dymnikov, V. P., Wallace, J. M., & Bladé, I. (1999). The effective number of spatial degrees of freedom of a time-varying field. Journal of Climate, 12, 1990-2009.
# Cangelosi, R., & Goriely, A. (2007). Component retention in principal component analysis with application to cDNA microarray data. Biology Direct, 2, 2.
# Cheverud, J. M. (2001). A simple correction for multiple comparisons in interval mapping genome scans. Heredity, 87, 52-58.
# Del Giudice, M. (2020). Effective dimensionality: A tutorial. Multivariate Behavioral Research. https://doi.org/10.1080/00273171.2020.1743631
# Fraedrich, K., Ziehmann, C., & Sielmann, F. (1995). Estimates of spatial degrees of freedom. Journal of Climate, 8, 361-369.
# Gnedenko, B., & Yelnik, I. (2016). Minimum entropy as a measure of effective dimensionality. SSRN, doi: 10.2139/ssrn.2767549.
# Higham, N. J. (2002). Computing the nearest correlation matrix—a problem from finance. IMA journal of Numerical Analysis, 22, 329-343.
# Kirkpatrick, M. (2009). Patterns of quantitative genetic variation in multiple dimensions. Genetica, 136, 271-284.
# Ledoit, O., & Wolf, M. (2012). Nonlinear shrinkage estimation of large-dimensional covariance matrices. Annals of Statistics, 40, 1024-1060.
# Ledoit, O., & Wolf, M. (2015). Spectrum estimation: A unified framework for covariance matrix estimation and PCA in large dimensions. Journal of Multivariate Analysis, 139, 360-384.
# Pirkl, R. J., Remley, K. A., & Patané, C. S. L. (2012). Reverberation chamber measurement correlation. IEEE Transactions on Electromagnetic Compatibility, 54, 533-545.
# Ramprasad, P. (2016). nlshrink v. 1.0.1. URL: https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=nlshrink
# Roy, O., & Vetterli, M. (2007). The effective rank: A measure of effective dimensionality. In M. Domański, R. Stasiński, & M. Bartkowiak (Eds.), 15th European Signal Processing Conference (pp. 606-610). Poznań, Poland: PTETiS.



# function estimate.ED (x, sample.size = NULL, rel.values = NULL, cov.mat = FALSE, small.sample.c = FALSE, round.digits = 2, print.summary = TRUE)
#
# Arguments
#
# x					data frame or correlation/covariance matrix
# sample.size		sample size (optional: required for small-sample bias correction from a correlation/covariance matrix)
# rel.values		vector of reliability coefficients (optional: only for disattenuation)
# cov.mat			if TRUE, ED estimators are computed from the covariance matrix; if FALSE (default), from the correlation matrix
# small.sample.c	if TRUE (default), the function returns estimators corrected for small-sample bias
# round.digits		rounding digits for the output (default is 2)
# print.summary		if TRUE (default), the function prints a summary of the analysis before returning the results
#
# Value
# returns a list object containing some or all of the following:
#
# n1				ED estimator based on the Shannon entropy H1 
# n2				ED estimator based on the quadratic entropy H2 
# nInf				ED estimator based on the min-entropy H_Inf; extremely conservative, not recommended
# nC				ED estimator by Cheverud (2001); not recommended
# n1.c				n1 corrected for small-sample bias
# n2.c				n2 corrected for small-sample bias
# nInf.c			nInf corrected for small-sample bias
# nC.c				nC corrected for small-sample bias



library(rootSolve)
library(nlshrink)
library(Matrix)

estimate.ED <- function (x, sample.size = NULL, rel.values = NULL, cov.mat = FALSE, small.sample.c = FALSE, round.digits = 2, print.summary = TRUE) {

indefinite.matrix = FALSE

########## check the input format, compute the correlation or covariance matrix

if (is.data.frame(x) == TRUE) {
	sample.size = nrow(x)
	
	if (cov.mat == FALSE) {
		matrix = cor(x, use="pairwise.complete.obs")
	}
	else matrix = cov(x, use="pairwise.complete.obs")
}
else {
	matrix = x

	if ( ((sum(diag(matrix)) != nrow(matrix) ) | (var(diag(matrix)) != 0)) & (cov.mat == FALSE) ) {  # checks if the matrix is a covariance matrix
		matrix = cov2cor(matrix)
	}	
}

########## disattenuate the correlation matrix if a vector of reliabilities has been supplied

if ( (cov.mat == FALSE) & (is.null(rel.values) == FALSE) ) {
	rel.matrix = sqrt(crossprod(t(rel.values), t(rel.values)))
	diag(rel.matrix) = 1
	matrix = matrix/rel.matrix
}
	
output = list()

########## check if the matrix is indefinite; if so, find the nearest positive definite matrix

if (sum(eigen(matrix)$values < 0) > 0) {
	indefinite.matrix = TRUE
	matrix = nearPD(matrix, corr=!cov.mat)$mat
}

########## find the eigenvalues, sort them in ASCENDING order for later computations

eigen_val = sort(eigen(matrix)$values)

eigen_val.c = NULL

########## correct the eigenvalues for small-sample bias 

if (small.sample.c == TRUE) {

	if (is.data.frame(x) == TRUE) {   #  from raw data: nonlinear shrinkage by Ledoit & Wolf 2012, 2015
			
		if(cov.mat == FALSE) {
			
			if(is.null(rel.values) == TRUE) {
				suppress = file()
				sink(file = suppress)  #  suppresses the print output from tau_estimate()
				tmp = tau_estimate(as.matrix(scale(x)))
				sink()
				close(suppress)
				eigen_val.c = tmp
			}
			else {  #  disattenuation
				sink("NUL")  #  suppresses the print output from tau_estimate()
				tmp = nlshrink_cov(as.matrix(scale(x)))
				sink()
				matrix.c = tmp/rel.matrix  #   disattenuate the corrected correlation matrix
				if (sum(eigen(matrix.c)$values < 0) > 0) {
					indefinite.matrix = TRUE
					matrix.c = nearPD(matrix.c, corr=TRUE)$mat  #  check if the matrix is indefinite, find the nearest positive definite matrix
				}
				eigen_val.c = sort(eigen(matrix.c)$values)
			}
		}	
		else {
			suppress = file()
			sink(file = suppress)  #  suppresses the print output from tau_estimate()
			tmp = tau_estimate(as.matrix(x))
			sink()
			close(suppress)
			eigen_val.c = tmp			
		}
		
	}
	else if (is.null(sample.size) == FALSE) {   #  from correlation/covariance matrix: correction by Mestre 2008
				
		eigen_val.rounded = round(eigen_val, 6)  #  to avoid errors when detecting duplicates
		eigen_val.c = eigen_val
			
		function.body = paste(eigen_val.rounded[1],"/(",eigen_val.rounded[1],"-x)")  #  build equation to find mu values
		for(index in 2:length(eigen_val.rounded)) {
			function.body = paste(function.body, "+",eigen_val.rounded[index],"/(",eigen_val.rounded[index],"-x)" )
		}
		function.body = paste(function.body,"-",sample.size)
		
		eval(parse(text = paste("f = function(x) {", function.body,"}")))
		
		unique.eigen = sum(!duplicated(eigen_val.rounded[eigen_val.rounded != 0]) )  #   number of unique nonzero eigenvalues
		
		mu_val = uniroot.all(f, interval=c(0, max(eigen_val.rounded)), n=10000000)  #  find mu values
		mu_val = mu_val[which( abs(f(mu_val)) %in% sort(abs(f(mu_val)))[1:unique.eigen]  ) ]   
		mu.index = 1
			for (index in 1:length(eigen_val.rounded)) {   
				
				if (eigen_val.rounded[index] != 0) {   # correct nonzero eigenvalues
					if (duplicated(eigen_val.rounded)[index] == FALSE) {
						eigen_val.c[index] = sample.size * (eigen_val.rounded[index] - mu_val[mu.index])
						mu.index = mu.index + 1
					}
					else {
						eigen_val.c[index] = eigen_val.c[index-1]
						}
				}
			}
	}

}

########## compute ED estimators

K = length(eigen_val)	
eigen_sum = sum(eigen_val)
norm_eigen_val = eigen_val/eigen_sum
eigen_var = var(eigen_val)*((K-1)/K)

 
output$n1 = prod(norm_eigen_val^(-norm_eigen_val))  
output$n2 = (eigen_sum^2)/sum(eigen_val^2) 
output$nInf = eigen_sum/max(eigen_val)    
output$nC = K - ((K^2)/(eigen_sum^2))*eigen_var  

if ( (small.sample.c == TRUE) & (is.null(eigen_val.c) == FALSE) ) {  # estimators corrected for small-sample bias
	eigen_sum.c = sum(eigen_val.c)
	norm_eigen_val.c = eigen_val.c/eigen_sum.c
	eigen_var.c = var(eigen_val.c)*((K-1)/K)

 	output$n1.c = max(prod(norm_eigen_val.c^(-norm_eigen_val.c)), output$n1)
	output$n2.c = max((eigen_sum.c^2)/sum(eigen_val.c^2), output$n2)
	output$nInf.c = max(eigen_sum.c/max(eigen_val.c), output$nInf) 
	output$nC.c = max(K - ((K^2)/(eigen_sum.c^2))*eigen_var.c, output$nC) 
}

########## print summary of the analysis if requested

if (print.summary == TRUE) {

	description = "ED estimated from the"
	if (cov.mat == TRUE) {description = paste(description, "covariance matrix;")}
	else {description = paste(description, "correlation matrix;")}
	if (is.null(rel.values) == FALSE) {description = paste(description, "disattenuated;")}
	else {description = paste(description, "no disattenuation;")}
	if ( (small.sample.c == TRUE) & (is.null(eigen_val.c) == FALSE) ) {
		if (is.data.frame(x) == TRUE) {description = paste(description, "corrected for small-sample bias (Ledoit & Wolf 2015).")}
		else {description = paste(description, "corrected for small-sample bias (Mestre 2008).")}
	}
	else {description = paste(description, "no small-sample correction.")}
	if (indefinite.matrix == TRUE) {description = paste(description, "Warning: an indefinite matrix was detected and replaced with the nearest positive definite matrix.")} 
	
	print(description, quote = FALSE)
	cat("\n")
}

########## return output list

return(lapply(output,round,round.digits))
}

```


```{r make_matrices}

countries <- unique(ipip$country)

cov_matrices <- list()
cor_matrices <- list()
sample_sizes <- list()

for(i in 1:length(countries)){
  
  current_country <- countries[i]

  
  latent_covs_corrs <- # get just estimates of factor covariances and correlations from alignment
    covariances %>% 
    filter(iso2 == current_country) %>% # filter to current country
    select(pair, covariance, correlation) %>% 
    mutate(pair = paste0(pair, "_")) # for easier identificaion later on
  
  latent_variances <- # get just estimates of factor variances from alignment
    variances %>% 
    filter(iso2 == current_country) %>% # might need to remove the fixed country
    select(factor = param, variance = est) # for easier identificaion later on
  
  # make empty square matrices to fill later
  latent_corrmat <- # assign for correlation matrix
    matrix(NA, 5, 5, # 5 by 5 matrix with all NA
           # give rows and columns names for easier id later
           dimnames = list(c("O", "C", "A", "E", "ES"), 
                           c("O", "C", "A", "E", "ES")))
  latent_covmat <- latent_corrmat #assign the same empty matrix for covariance matrix
  
  combos <- combn(dimnames(latent_corrmat)[[1]], 2) # all the pairwise combos
  
  # loop to put correct values in the correct cells of entry matrix
  for(j in 1:ncol(combos)){
    
    row <- combos[1, j]
    column <- combos[2, j]
    
    # pattern for matching in any order later on later 
    pattern <- paste0(paste(row, column, sep = "_"), "_|", paste(column, row, sep = "_"), "_")
    
    # make correlation matrix with 1s on the diagonal
    # put each pairwise correlation in the correct row/column combination
    latent_corrmat[row, column] <- latent_covs_corrs[grepl(pattern, latent_covs_corrs$pair), 
                                                     "correlation"]
    latent_corrmat[column, row] <- latent_covs_corrs[grepl(pattern, latent_covs_corrs$pair), 
                                                     "correlation"]
    
    # put 1s on the diagonal (all the remaining NA values)
    latent_corrmat[is.na(latent_corrmat)] <- 1
    
    
    # make covariance matrix with factor variances on the diagonal
    # put each pairwise covariance in the correct row/column combination
    latent_covmat[row, column] <- latent_covs_corrs[grepl(pattern, latent_covs_corrs$pair), 
                                                    "covariance"]
    latent_covmat[column, row] <- latent_covs_corrs[grepl(pattern, latent_covs_corrs$pair), 
                                                    "covariance"]
    # put variances on the diagonal
    latent_covmat[column, column] <- latent_variances[which(latent_variances$factor == column), 
                                                      "variance"]
    
    latent_covmat[row, row] <- latent_variances[which(latent_variances$factor == row), 
                                                "variance"]
  }
  

  cor_matrices[[current_country]] <- latent_corrmat  
  cov_matrices[[current_country]] <- latent_covmat  
  

}

```


```{r effective_dimensionality, eval=T}

n1s <- list()

for(i in 1:length(countries)){
  
  current_country <- countries[i]

  country_N <- subset(covariances, iso2 == current_country)[1, "N"]
  
  covmat <- cov_matrices[[current_country]]
  
  # effective dimensionality analysis with sample size correction
  ED_results <- estimate.ED(covmat, sample.size = country_N, 
                            small.sample.c = T, # apply correction for small sample bias
                            print.summary = F)

  n1s[[current_country]] <- ED_results$n1.c
  
  # save the results lists on each loop
  save(n1s, file = "data/ED_results.Rdata")

}
```

```{r results}
                                           destination = "iso3n")) %>% 
  left_join(country_data) %>% # country ID to join by 
  full_join(means %>% rename(iso3_n = Group)) %>% 
  mutate(Asia = ifelse(continent == "Asia", 1, 0),
         Africa = ifelse(continent == "Africa", 1, 0),
         Oceania = ifelse(continent == "Oceania", 1, 0),
         Americas = ifelse(continent == "Americas", 1, 0),
         n1s_notscaled = n1s,
         niche_diversity_notscaled = niche_diversity) %>% 
  mutate_at(., .vars = c("n1s", "niche_diversity", "logN", "acquiescence",
                         "homicide_rate", "mortality", "EPI",
                         "eci", "hdi", "urban_pop",
                         "A_mean", "C_mean", "E_mean", "ES_mean", "O_mean",
                         "Asia",  "Africa", "Oceania", "Americas"),
            .funs = scale)
```

### Pairwise Facets

```{r pairwise_facets}

root_path <- "mplus/MetaRegression/" # for shorter file paths

metareg_covariance_pairwise_mplus <- 
  covariances %>% 
  select(pair, covariance, correlation, se, niche_diversity, iso3n = Group, 
         # control variables
         continent, # keep continent dummy codes
         # control variables
         N, logN, acquiescence, hdi, urban_pop, eci,  
         homicide_rate, mortality, EPI,
         contains("mean")) %>% # mean IPIP factor scores for each country
  gather(key = estimate_type, value = estimate, correlation, covariance) %>% 
  filter(!is.na(pair)) %>% 
  unite("pair", pair, estimate_type) %>% 
    mutate(iso3n = as.numeric(iso3n), 
         acquiescence = as.numeric(acquiescence),
         estimate = abs(estimate), 
         # Dummy codes with Europe as intercept
         Asia = ifelse(continent == "Asia", 1, 0),
         Africa = ifelse(continent == "Africa", 1, 0),
         Oceania = ifelse(continent == "Oceania", 1, 0),
         Americas = ifelse(continent == "Americas", 1, 0),
         num_continent = as.numeric(factor(continent))-1) %>% 
  select(-continent) %>% 
  pivot_wider(names_from = pair, values_from = estimate)

# save data for use in metareg
prepareMplusData(metareg_covariance_pairwise_mplus, 
                 paste(root_path,
                       "pairwise_covariances/metareg_covariance_pairwise_mplus.dat",
                       sep = ""))


metareg_variance_facets_mplus <- 
  variances %>% 
  filter(Group != 840) %>%  # (s.e. of 0 causes divide by zero error)
  select(param, est, se, niche_diversity, iso3n = Group, 
         # control variables
         continent, # keep continent dummy codes
         # control variables
         N, logN, acquiescence, hdi, urban_pop, eci, 
         homicide_rate, mortality, EPI,
         contains("mean")) %>% # mean IPIP factor scores for each country
  mutate(iso3n = as.numeric(iso3n), 
         acquiescence = as.numeric(acquiescence),
         # Dummy codes with Europe as intercept
         Asia = ifelse(continent == "Asia", 1, 0),
         Africa = ifelse(continent == "Africa", 1, 0),
         Oceania = ifelse(continent == "Oceania", 1, 0),
         Americas = ifelse(continent == "Americas", 1, 0),
         num_continent = as.numeric(factor(continent))-1) %>% 
  select(-continent) %>% 
  spread(param, est)

# save data for use in metareg
prepareMplusData(metareg_variance_facets_mplus, 
                 paste(root_path,
                 "individual_factor_variances/metareg_variance_facets_mplus.dat",
                 sep = ""))
```

```{r pairwise_plots}

all_pairs_output <- readModels(target = "mplus/MetaRegression/pairwise_covariances/")
all_pairs_results <- list()
pairs_point_estimates <- list()

for(i in 1:length(all_pairs_output)){
  current_pair_results <- all_pairs_output[[i]]
  current_pair_name <- names(all_pairs_output)[i]
  
  all_pairs_results[[current_pair_name]] <- 
  current_pair_results$parameters$unstandardized %>% 
  data.frame() %>% 
  filter(paramHeader == "New.Additional.Parameters")
  
  pairs_point_estimates[[current_pair_name]] <- 
  current_pair_results$parameters$stdyx.standardized %>% 
  data.frame() %>% 
  filter(param == "SC")

  
  
}

point_estimates_no_controls <- 
  bind_rows(pairs_point_estimates, .id = "pair") %>% 
  filter(grepl(".ON",paramHeader)) %>% 
  separate(pair, into = c("pair", NA), sep = "\\.") %>% 
  select(pair, point_est = est, pvalue = pval, point_se = se)

factor_pairwise_covariances_results <- 
  bind_rows(all_pairs_results, .id = "pair") %>% 
  filter(!grepl(".ON",paramHeader)) %>% 
  separate(pair, into = c("pair", NA), sep = "\\.") %>% 
  full_join(point_estimates_no_controls) %>% 
  mutate(uci = est + 1.96*se, # upper confidience interval 
         lci = est - 1.96*se, # upper confidience interval
         niche_diversity = ifelse(param == "SC_LOW", -2.5, 
                     ifelse(param == "SC_HIGH", 3.1, 
                            0))) %>% 
  mutate(pvalue = ifelse(pvalue < .001, paste("p < .001"), 
                         paste("p = ", weights::rd(pvalue, digits = 3), sep = "")),
         point_est = weights::rd(point_est, digits = 2)) %>% 
  mutate(pair_order = fct_reorder(pair, point_est, .desc = T))
```

# Supplemental Analyses

## Individual components of the niche diversity index and stepwise control sets

Here we present the relationships between each individual variable within the niche diversity index (i.e., sectoral diversity, urbanization, and HDI) and the focal outcomes (i.e., inter-factor covariance, intra-factor variance, and effective dimensionality) in order to exam whether the observed relationships for the niche diversity composite are driven by any one of its components. Moreover, we examined the effects of different sets of controls entered in a stepwise fashion, with methodological controls only, then with the addition of environmental harshness (EH) indictors (i.e., mortality and homicide rates), and finally with the geospatial controls as well.

### Inter-factor covariance from individual niche diversity variables and different control sets

```{r covariance_individual, include=F}

niche_diversity_vars <- c("niche_diversity", # niche diversity composite
                          "eci", # sectoral diversity
                          "urban_pop", # percentage of people living in cities
                          "hdi" # human development index
                          )

ind_cov_results <- list()
ind_cov_controls_results <- list()
ind_cov_methcontrols_results <- list()
ind_cov_LHcontrols_results <- list()
ind_cov_methLHcontrols_results <- list()

for(i in 1:length(niche_diversity_vars)){
```

```{r covariance_allmodelresults_table, echo=F}
                        "C_MEAN" = "Conscientiousness",
                        "E_MEAN" = "Extraversion",
                        "ES_MEAN" = "Emotional Stability",
                        "O_MEAN" = "Openness",
                        "LOGN" = "Sample Size",
                        "ACQUIESCEN" = "Acquiescence",
                        "HOMICIDE_R" = "Homicide Rate",
                        "MORTALITY" = "Mortality Rate",
                        "EPI" = "English Proficiency",
                        "ASIA" = "Asia",
                        "AFRICA" = "Africa",
                        "OCEANIA" = "Oceania",
                        "AMERICAS" = "Americas"),
         CI = paste0(low2.5, ", ", up2.5)
         ) %>% 
  arrange(control) %>% 
  select(model, param:pval, CI) %>% 
  mutate(pval = ifelse(pval <= 0.000, "< .001", pval)) %>% 
  kbl(format = "html",
      col.names = c("Focal Predictor (Control Set)", "Parameter", "$\\beta$", "$\\textit{SE}$", "$\\textit{p}$", "95% CI"),

  kable_paper("striped", full_width = T) %>%
  collapse_rows(1, valign = "top", target = 1) %>% 
  scroll_box(width = "100%", height = "750px")
```

### Effective dimensionality from individual niche diversity variables and different control sets

```{r ED_individual, include=F}

ind_ED_results <- list()
ind_ED_allcontrols <- list()
ind_ED_methcontrols <- list()
ind_ED_methLHcontrols <- list()

for(i in 1:length(niche_diversity_vars)){
  
  current <- niche_diversity_vars[[i]] # assign the current individual variable
  
  ed_model_base <- lm(n1s ~ get(current), 
                      data = ed_analysis_df)
  
  result_df <- data.frame(
    cbind(summary(ed_model_base)$coefficients[,-3], 
          confint(ed_model_base), 
          nrow(ed_model_base$model)))[2, ]
  
  names(result_df) <- names(cleaned_var_results %>% select(est:NClusters))
  rownames(result_df) <- NULL
  
  ind_ED_results[[current]] <- result_df
  
  # all controls
  ed_model_allcontrols <- 
  lm(n1s ~ get(current) + 
       # methods controls
       logN + acquiescence + EPI + A_mean + C_mean + E_mean + ES_mean + O_mean +
       # environmental harshness
       homicide_rate + mortality + 
       # regional
       Asia + Africa + Oceania + Americas, 
     data = ed_analysis_df)

  result_df <- data.frame(
    cbind(summary(ed_model_allcontrols)$coefficients[,-3], 
          confint(ed_model_allcontrols), 
          nrow(ed_model_allcontrols$model)))
  
  names(result_df) <- names(cleaned_var_results %>% select(est:NClusters))

  ind_ED_allcontrols[[current]] <- result_df %>% rownames_to_column(., "param")
  
  # methods controls
  ed_model_allcontrols <- 
  lm(n1s ~ get(current) + 
       # methods controls
       logN + acquiescence + EPI + A_mean + C_mean + E_mean + ES_mean + O_mean,
     data = ed_analysis_df)

  result_df <- data.frame(
    cbind(summary(ed_model_allcontrols)$coefficients[,-3], 
          confint(ed_model_allcontrols), 
          nrow(ed_model_allcontrols$model)))
  
  names(result_df) <- names(cleaned_var_results %>% select(est:NClusters))

  ind_ED_methcontrols[[current]] <- result_df %>% rownames_to_column(., "param")
  
  
  # methods controls
  ed_model_allcontrols <- 
  lm(n1s ~ get(current) + 
       # methods controls
       logN + acquiescence + EPI + A_mean + C_mean + E_mean + ES_mean + O_mean +
       # environmental harshness
       homicide_rate + mortality,
     data = ed_analysis_df)

  result_df <- data.frame(
    cbind(summary(ed_model_allcontrols)$coefficients[,-3], 
          confint(ed_model_allcontrols), 
          nrow(ed_model_allcontrols$model))) 
  
  names(result_df) <- names(cleaned_var_results %>% select(est:NClusters))

  ind_ED_methLHcontrols[[current]] <- result_df %>% rownames_to_column(., "param")
    

}
```

```{r effectivedimensionality_allresults_table, echo=F}
                                              "Methods Controls Only",
                                              "Methods + EH Controls",
                                              "All Controls")),
         model = paste0(predictor, " (", control, ")"),
         param = recode(param,
                       # "niche_diversity" = "Niche Diversity Index",
                       "logN" = "Sample Size",
                       "acquiescence" = "Acquiescence",
                       "homicide_rate" = "Homicide Rate",
                       "mortality" = "Mortality Rate",
                       "EPI" = "English Proficiency",
                       "A_mean" = "Agreeableness",
                       "C_mean" = "Conscientiousness",
                       "E_mean" = "Extraversion", 
                       "ES_mean" = "Emotional Stability",
                       "O_mean" = "Openness"),
         pval = round(pval, 3), est = round(est, 3), se = round(se, 3), 
         low2.5 = round(low2.5, 3),up2.5 = round(up2.5, 3),
         CI = paste0(low2.5, ", ", up2.5)
         ) %>% 
  arrange(control) %>% 
  select(model, param, est:pval, CI) %>% 
  mutate(pval = ifelse(pval <= 0.000, "< .001", pval)) %>% 
  kbl(format = "html",
      col.names = c("Focal Predictor (Control Set)", "Parameter", "$\\beta$", "$\\textit{SE}$", "$\\textit{p}$", "95% CI"),
      align = c("l", "l", "c", "c", "c", "c")) %>% 
  kable_paper("striped", full_width = T) %>%
  collapse_rows(1, valign = "top", target = 1) %>% 
  scroll_box(width = "100%", height = "750px")
```

## Comparison with and without multigroup alignment method

Here, we compare the results of analyses based on inter-factor covariances and intra-factor variances estimated from simple factor mean-scores with those based on the multigroup alignment method The covariance and variance estimates based on the simple factor mean-scores did not exhibit enough systematic variability to conduct the metaregression analyses (Mplus estimates the nation-level variability as zero). We therefore conducted single-level regression analyses on the aggregated inter-factor covariance and the intra-factor variance estimates for each nation. This aggregation approach was used in Lukaszewski et al. (2016) and Smaldino et al. (2019). For comparison, we report these single-level regression analyses alongside single-level regression analyses using aggregated *alignment*-estimated inter-factor covariances and intra-factor variances as well (rather than the metaregression analyses reported in the main text). Differences between the results under the different approach can be attributed to a combination of measurement error and measurement non-invariance (bias).

```{r calculatefactorscores}

# get simple factor mean-scores
simple_factor_scores <- 
  ipip %>% # the cleaned IPIP data
  # Calculate the means of items for each personality trait
  # (these are already correctly reverse coded)
  mutate(O = rowMeans(select(., OPN1:OPN10), na.rm = T), # mean of openness items
         C = rowMeans(select(., CSN1:CSN10), na.rm = T), # mean of conscientiousness items
         E = rowMeans(select(., EXT1:EXT10), na.rm = T),
         A = rowMeans(select(., AGR1:AGR10), na.rm = T),
         ES = rowMeans(select(., EST1:EST10), na.rm = T)) %>% 
  # keep just the country info and the mean personality scores
  select(country, O, C, E, A, ES)

```

### Inter-factor covariance

```{r interfactor_correlations_simple}

# get covariance and correlation estimates from simple scores
simple_interfactor_covs_corrs <- 
  simple_factor_scores %>% # these are the mean factor scores for each person 
  group_by(country) %>% # groups by country to calculate country-level corrs easily
  summarise(O_C = cor(O, C, # calculate cor between O_C in each country
                      use = "pairwise.complete"), 
            O_E = cor(O, E, use = "pairwise.complete"), # calculate O_E cor in each country
            O_A = cor(O, A, use = "pairwise.complete"), # ...
            O_ES = cor(O, ES, use = "pairwise.complete"),
            C_E = cor(C, E, use = "pairwise.complete"),
            C_A = cor(C, A, use = "pairwise.complete"),
            C_ES = cor(C, ES, use = "pairwise.complete"),
            E_A = cor(E, A, use = "pairwise.complete"),
            E_ES = cor(E, ES, use = "pairwise.complete"), 
            A_ES = cor(A, ES, use = "pairwise.complete"),
            n = n()) %>% 
  gather(key = pair, value = correlation, -country, -n) %>% 
  mutate(se = sqrt((1-correlation^2)/(n-2))) %>%
  # join with the same thing but covariances instead of correlations
  full_join(simple_factor_scores %>% 
      group_by(country) %>% 
      summarise(O_C = cov(O, C, use = "pairwise.complete"),
                O_E = cov(O, E, use = "pairwise.complete"),
                O_A = cov(O, A, use = "pairwise.complete"),
                O_ES = cov(O, ES, use = "pairwise.complete"),
                C_E = cov(C, E, use = "pairwise.complete"),
                C_A = cov(C, A, use = "pairwise.complete"),
                C_ES = cov(C, ES, use = "pairwise.complete"),
                E_A = cov(E, A, use = "pairwise.complete"),
                E_ES = cov(E, ES, use = "pairwise.complete"), 
                A_ES = cov(A, ES, use = "pairwise.complete"),
                n = n()) %>% 
      gather(key = pair, value = cov, -country, -n)
  ) %>% 
  rename(iso2 = country) %>% 
  # # join with country level data
  right_join(country_data, by = "iso2")
    
```

```{r covariance_data_aggregation}
# aggregate absolute values of covariances from simple scores
covariance_df <-
  simple_interfactor_covs_corrs %>%
               group_by(iso3, country, continent, niche_diversity) %>%
               summarise(covariance = mean(abs(cov))) %>% 
  na.omit %>% ungroup() %>% 
  full_join(country_data) %>% full_join(means %>% mutate(iso3n = as.numeric(Group))) 

# aggregate absolute values of covariances from alignment scores
alignment_covariance_df <- 
  metareg_covariance_mplusdata %>% 
  group_by(iso3n, niche_diversity, logN) %>% 
  summarise(covariance = mean(abscov)) %>% 
  full_join(country_data) %>% full_join(means %>% mutate(iso3n = as.numeric(Group))) %>% 
  ungroup()

```

#### Comparison without controls

The negative association between niche diversity and average inter-factor covariance is larger under the alignment-based analyses than the simple factor mean-score analyses (see scatterplot and regression tables below).

```{r plot_covariance_simple}
  full_join(alignment_covariance_df %>% 
              select(iso3n, Alignment_covariance = covariance), 
            by = "iso3n") %>% 
  gather(key = method, value = covariance, 
         c(FactorMeans_covariance, Alignment_covariance)) %>% 
  group_by(method) %>% mutate(covariance = scale(covariance)) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = niche_diversity, y = covariance, color = method)) + 
  geom_smooth(method = "lm") +
  geom_point(alpha = .7) +
```


### Intra-factor variance 

```{r factor_variances_simple, include=T, eval = T}

# get variance estimates based on simple mean scores
simple_factor_variances <- 
  simple_factor_scores %>% # these are the mean factor scores for each person 
  group_by(country) %>% # groups by country to calculate country-level sd easily
  summarise(O = sd(O, na.rm = T), # gets the standard deviation of O for each country
            C = sd(C, na.rm = T), # gets the standard deviation of C for each country
            E = sd(E, na.rm = T), # ...
            A = sd(A, na.rm = T),
            ES = sd(ES, na.rm = T),
            n = n()) %>% # gets N for each country
  gather(key = factor, value = sd, -country, -n) %>% # converts to long (for mplus clustering)
  # convert to variance and calculate se of variance
  # se of variance = variance * sqrt(2 / (n -1))
  # se formula from : https://web.eecs.umich.edu/~fessler/papers/files/tr/stderr.pdf
  mutate(variance = sd^2, # variance
         se = variance * (sqrt(2 / (n - 1)))) %>% # caclulate se
  rename(iso2 = country) %>% 
  # join with country level data
  right_join(country_data, by = "iso2") 

```

```{r variance_data_aggregation}

# aggregate simple variance estimates 
variance_df <-
  simple_factor_variances %>%
               group_by(iso3, country, continent, niche_diversity) %>%
               summarise(variance = mean(variance)) %>% na.omit %>% ungroup() %>% 
  full_join(country_data) %>% full_join(means %>% mutate(iso3n = as.numeric(Group))) 

# aggregate alignment variance estimates
alignment_variance_df <- 
  metareg_variance_mplusdata %>% 
  group_by(iso3n, niche_diversity, logN) %>% 
  summarise(variance = mean(variance)) %>% 
  full_join(country_data) %>% full_join(means %>% mutate(iso3n = as.numeric(Group))) %>% 
  ungroup()

```

```{r plot_variance_simple}
  geom_smooth(method = "lm") +
  geom_point(alpha = .7) +
  xlab("Niche Diveristy") + ylab("Mean Intra-factor Variance") +
```

### Effective Dimensionality

```{r make_matrices_simple}

# make matrices for the effective dimensionality analyses

countries <- unique(ipip$country)

cov_matrices <- list()
cor_matrices <- list()
sample_sizes <- list()

for(i in 1:length(countries)){
  
  current_country <- countries[i]

  
  latent_covs_corrs <- # get just estimates of factor covariances and correlations from alignment
    simple_interfactor_covs_corrs %>% 
    filter(iso2 == current_country) %>% # filter to current country
    select(pair, covariance = cov, correlation) %>% 
    mutate(pair = paste0(pair, "_")) # for easier identificaion later on
  
  latent_variances <- # get just estimates of factor variances from alignment
    simple_factor_variances %>% 
    filter(iso2 == current_country) %>% # might need to remove the fixed country
    select(factor, variance) # for easier identificaion later on
  
  # make empty square matrices to fill later
  latent_corrmat <- # assign for correlation matrix
    matrix(NA, 5, 5, # 5 by 5 matrix with all NA
           # give rows and columns names for easier id later
           dimnames = list(c("O", "C", "A", "E", "ES"), 
                           c("O", "C", "A", "E", "ES")))
  latent_covmat <- latent_corrmat #assign the same empty matrix for covariance matrix
  
  combos <- combn(dimnames(latent_corrmat)[[1]], 2) # all the pairwise combos
  
  # loop to put correct values in the correct cells of entry matrix
  for(j in 1:ncol(combos)){
    
    row <- combos[1, j]
    column <- combos[2, j]
    
    # pattern for matching in any order later on later 
    pattern <- paste0(paste(row, column, sep = "_"), "_|", paste(column, row, sep = "_"), "_")
    
    # make correlation matrix with 1s on the diagonal
    # put each pairwise correlation in the correct row/column combination
    latent_corrmat[row, column] <- latent_covs_corrs[grepl(pattern, latent_covs_corrs$pair), 
                                                     "correlation"] %>% pull
    latent_corrmat[column, row] <- latent_covs_corrs[grepl(pattern, latent_covs_corrs$pair), 
                                                     "correlation"] %>% pull
    
    # put 1s on the diagonal (all the remaining NA values)
    latent_corrmat[is.na(latent_corrmat)] <- 1
    
    
    # make covariance matrix with factor variances on the diagonal
    # put each pairwise covariance in the correct row/column combination
    latent_covmat[row, column] <- latent_covs_corrs[grepl(pattern, latent_covs_corrs$pair), 
                                                    "covariance"] %>% pull
    latent_covmat[column, row] <- latent_covs_corrs[grepl(pattern, latent_covs_corrs$pair), 
                                                    "covariance"] %>% pull
    # put variances on the diagonal
    latent_covmat[column, column] <- latent_variances[which(latent_variances$factor == column), 
                                                      "variance"] %>% pull
    
    latent_covmat[row, row] <- latent_variances[which(latent_variances$factor == row), 
                                                "variance"] %>% pull
  }
  

  cor_matrices[[current_country]] <- latent_corrmat  
  cov_matrices[[current_country]] <- latent_covmat  
  

}

```

```{r effective_dimensionality_simple}

# calculate effective dimensionality in each country
n1s <- list()

for(i in 1:length(countries)){
  
  current_country <- countries[i]

  country_N <- subset(simple_interfactor_covs_corrs, 
                      iso2 == current_country)[1, "N"] %>% pull
  
  covmat <- cov_matrices[[current_country]]
  
  # effective dimensionality analysis with sample size correction
  ED_results <- estimate.ED(covmat, sample.size = country_N, 
                            small.sample.c = T, # apply correction for small sample bias
                            print.summary = F)

  n1s[[current_country]] <- ED_results$n1.c
  
  # save the results lists on each loop
  save(n1s, file = "data/ED_results_simple.Rdata")

}

```

```{r simple_ED_results}
                               destination = "country.name"),

                                           destination = "iso3n")) %>%

         Americas = ifelse(continent == "Americas", 1, 0),

                         "A_mean", "C_mean", "E_mean", "ES_mean", "O_mean",
                         "Asia",  "Africa", "Oceania", "Americas"),
            .funs = scale)
```


## CFAs for each nation

```{r nation_cfa_loop, eval=F}


# list of included countries and Ns
country_include <- unique(ipip$country)

results <- list() # make empty list for results

for(i in 1:length(country_include)){ #begining of loop to run a CFA for each nation
  
ipip_CFA <- # create subset of current nation
	ipip %>%  
	filter(country == country_include[i]) %>% 
	select(EXT1:OPN10) 

# prepare for mplus and save
prepareMplusData(ipip_CFA, "mplus/CFA/CFA_data.dat")

# run the CFA model
runModels(target = paste(getwd(),"mplus/CFA/", sep = "/"), # need full file path
          replaceOutfile="always") 

# read and save results into the results list country name
results[[country_include[i]]] <- readModels(target = "mplus/CFA/CFA.out")$summaries

# save to csv to have live results
write.csv(bind_rows(results, .id = "country"), 
          "mplus/CFA/countryCFA_results.csv", row.names = F)

}

```

```{r cfa_results}
  filter(RMSEA_Estimate < .08) %>% pull(country)
```
